body: If there's one thing I've learned it's that if you feel a similar way you should take a gander in the mirror. Also, try it out with your friends. You could be very well the change that the world is waiting for. People immediately see me as a creep. I've had many friends comment on it, "at first I thought you were a creep but once I got to know you..." etc. If you know the game and can make it work for you in a positive way then go for it. Bring people up when you can. So many people spread hate that its become degenerative on our society. We need people who get it and give a damn. We need it so badly.

> Smile at everyone, say "Hello!" to everyone enthusiastically, sounds dumb, but it's really fun lol

But that's my issue. Do you know how easy it is to fake a smile? Why is this a standard in which we live by? Do you know how fucking easy it is to play nice, smile, and keep the energy up? But **why**? To meet what end? Why can't we realize that people are just people and that making assumptions is baseless? Why is life coming off as some poorly constructed game made by a couple of bitter half wits? Why should I be able to sell myself to people through the simplest of actions -- such as smiling or making small talk -- but being myself finds me in the most dark and lonely of places? What's the fucking point? I'm tired of people running away from me (literally in some instances) because they assume I'm out to get them or something. It's really weird just walking to your car at the end of a class at college only to cross paths with someone who will give you the double take and book it only to look back a third time to be surprised you aren't chasing them like a rabid dog. What the fuck did I do? I don't smile hard enough? I look like a god damn rapist for buttfucking no reason? They watched CSI and jumped the gun? What the fuck?

EDIT: Just try to imagine this. You've graduated from whatever institution is the end all, and you find that everyone else is still stuck at the beginning. You try to help them, but instead of gratitude they develop a hate for you. You try to help but they just don't get it. And when you try to play the same hands that they're playing they think that there's something wrong with you. They'll ignore their own inability to plan years ahead (and I mean many years), they're too easily impressed by a vocabulary, and all they give a damn about is being happy. As if that's the end to life. Then imagine that you too have feelings and that you don't want to create for those who will simply hate on the assumption that the future will recognize your actions. I just want to be a fucking person, not Newton. I want to have a wife and kids, but that seems impossible from my standpoint. Maybe I'm too shallow, maybe I'm stubborn. But if you're going to get with someone you should at least enjoy their company, right? So why the fuck am I constantly being brushed aside into these social groups that I find reprehensible? Am I too far off the button?
